summary.title: Design for Non-Designers — Beyond Tellerand Dusseldorf 2018
summary.one_liner: A talk-deck for developers and non-designers covering one core visual design principle, basic typography rules, image tips, and a beginner-friendly design process.
takeaways: Keep the number of fonts low, usually two, and use display fonts sparingly.
Create hierarchy by varying weight, style, and text transforms instead of adding more fonts.
Whitespace can improve results: the deck cites a Xerox case where removing extra links around Add to Cart buttons raised engagement by 20%.
Stock photos often look like stock photos, so choose carefully; type and screenshots can carry a lot.
Watch image file size and provide retina-quality images.
The talk outlines an overview of the design process to move from idea to execution quickly.
summary.summary: This is a Speaker Deck slide deck from a 2018 Beyond Tellerand Düsseldorf talk by designer Tracy (@limedaring) aimed at non-designers. It covers one core visual design principle and how it links to major design concepts, plus an overview of the design process for going from idea to execution. The slides also give concrete typography guidance (limit fonts, vary weight and style) and image tips (avoid generic stock photos, watch file size, use retina assets). The page text is mostly slide fragments, so detailed explanations of the process steps are not included.
